# jinx

> Nix, transpiled to TypeScript. This page is a playground: the Nix in
> the left pane is compiled to the TypeScript in the middle pane, which
> is evaluated in the tab into the value on the right. A `derivation`
> call produces the `.drv` Nix would, with the same drvPath and output
> paths. Nothing runs on a server.

## The URL is the state

The editor's contents live in the URL hash, so a snippet is a link:

- `#code=<base64>` the Nix source, UTF-8, base64-encoded (standard or
  URL-safe alphabet, padding optional)

The page rewrites the hash as the editor changes. With no hash the page
shows the "a derivation" example.

## Reading the page

The result is in the DOM. After a change the page waits 300 ms, then
compiles and evaluates:

- `#value` the value printed as `nix-instantiate --eval --strict` would,
  or the error (then it carries class `error`)
- `#json` the value as JSON, or a note that it has no JSON form
- `#derivations` one `article.drv` per derivation produced, with its
  name (`h3`), drvPath (`code.drv-path`), outputs (`dl.outputs`) and the
  ATerm (`pre.aterm`)
- `#status` "evaluated in N ms, N derivations", or the failure
- `#log` lines from `builtins.trace` and evaluation warnings

The TypeScript pane is read-only until the "edit" box (`#ts-edit`) is
checked; after that the pane's text is what gets evaluated and Nix edits
no longer overwrite it.

## Driving it

`window.jinx` is the compiler and runtime bundle (`site/js/jinx.js`,
built from `src/browser/playground.ts`):

- `jinx.compile(nix)` returns `{ ok: true, typescript }` or
  `{ ok: false, error }`
- `jinx.evaluate(typescript)` returns `{ ok: true, printed, json,
  derivations: [{ drvPath, name, aterm, outputs }], millis }` or
  `{ ok: false, error }`
- `jinx.evaluateNix(nix)` does both
- `jinx.configure({ system, log })` sets `builtins.currentSystem` and
  where trace output goes

`window.playground` is the page: `getNix()`, `setNix(text)`,
`getTypeScript()` and `run()`.

## The nixpkgs page

`/nixpkgs/` evaluates real nixpkgs in the tab: a worker
(`js/nixpkgs-worker.js`, built from `src/browser/nixpkgs-worker.ts`)
runs the compiled nixpkgs tree named by `nixpkgs/config.json`
(`treeUrl`, `srcUrl`, `rev`), fetching each module as the evaluation
reaches it. The state is the hash: `#attr=hello`, a dotted path for a
nested set (`#attr=python3Packages.requests`). The page evaluates the
package set once on load (`#status` reads "package set ready in ...",
then `#attr` and `#run` are enabled) and runs the attribute from the
hash. The result is in the DOM: `#result-card` with the name
(`#result-title`), `#drv-path`, `#outputs` (one line per output),
`#source` (the `.nix` on GitHub) and `#trynix-link`, whose href boots
the output path at trynix.dev; `#error-text` holds a failure; `#status`
reads "done in N ms" or "failed". `#activity` counts the modules, files
and bytes fetched so far.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/fzakaria/jinx): what it is and how it is
  put together
- [Design](https://github.com/fzakaria/jinx/blob/main/docs/design.md):
  the value mapping, where thunks go, what the emitted code looks like
- [Semantics](https://github.com/fzakaria/jinx/blob/main/docs/semantics.md):
  the language, as implemented
- [Verification](https://github.com/fzakaria/jinx/blob/main/docs/verification.md):
  the conformance suite and the whole-nixpkgs drvPath diff
- [Ideas](https://github.com/fzakaria/jinx/blob/main/docs/ideas.md):
  what a TypeScript nixpkgs makes possible
